title: feat(nuxt,vite-server): render the error page in the renderer itself
body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

<!-- Please ensure there is an open issue and mention its number. For example, "resolves #123" -->

### 📚 Description

currently, we perform a second render when there's an issue rendering. we encode the error in a query, and make a _fresh request_ to `/__nuxt_error` with this query, then render that error fresh.

this is one of the more idiosyncratic behaviours, although it did allow for clearly isolating error context

@pi0 has been suggesting for a while that it's a good idea for us to consider a simple try/catch around the renderer, and I agree....

this PR moves the error render into `fetch`; on the same event:

- the caught error is normalised, handed to `captureError` and `onDevError`, and we then render `error.vue` is with a fresh `NuxtSSRContext`
- we keep the headers and cookies the failed render had already written (for free, because it's the same event)
- we avoid having to track recursion as it's a simple try/catch 
- JSON requests _do_ throw and avoid the `error.vue` entirely

because this is a bigger change, it's gated behind `experimental.inlineErrorRendering`, which is enabled by default from `compatibilityVersion: 5`.

### 🚨 Bigger changes

this is intended to be non-breaking, but it's worth pointing out that:

- error renders don't go through Nitro middleware or route rules a second time
- `render:html` fires for the error page with the _original_ event, and `x-nitro-prerender` hints are also collected from the original event
- modules listening on Nitro's `error` hook still fire, through `captureError`
- `/__nuxt_error` is no longer fetched internally - we'll drop it in a future PR

all of these are correctness fixes but I wanted to mention them all the same...
